source_refs.note: Book p. 188-190: 6.4 Ellipse, definition, Kepler's first law, Figure 6.14, Derivation of the Standard Equation with Figure 6.15, Do You Know box

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum! Circle aur parabola ke baad ab hum teesre conic, yani ellipse, ki taraf aate hain. Ellipse ko aap rozmarra mein dekhte hain: anda (egg) aam taur par is jaisi shakal ka hota hai, jhuka hua paani ka glass dekhein to paani ki satah ellipse banti hai, aur planets Sun ke gird ellipse par hi ghoomte hain. Is sabaq mein hum pehle ellipse ki definition samjhenge, phir qadam ba qadam us ki standard equation khud derive karenge, taa ke formula ratta na lagana pare.

Kitab ki definition: ellipse plane ke un tamam points ka set hai jin ke do fixed points se faaslon ka jama (sum) hamesha ek hi constant rehta hai. In do fixed points ko foci kehte hain (focus ki jama). Kepler ka pehla qanoon (law) kehta hai ke solar system mein planets ke orbits (madaar) elliptical hain. Neeche Figure 6.14 dekhiye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "see Figure 14" likhti hai, magar murad Figure 6.14 hai (jo neeche di gayi hai). Sirf figure ka number adhoora chhapa hai.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par magenta ellipse, andar do foci F' (baayen) aur F (daayen). Ellipse ke upar baayen point P dono foci se cyan lines se jura hai, aur upar daayen doosra point P kaali lines se. Dono P ke liye PF' + PF barabar hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.14: the sum |PF'| + |PF| is the same for every point P (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.14)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ek chhota sa tajurba kijiye: ek board par do pins gaarein (yeh foci hain). Dhaage ka ek loop dono pins ke gird daalein, pencil se dhaaga tight kheenchein aur pencil ko poora ghuma dein. Dhaage ki lambai kabhi nahi badalti, is liye pencil ka dono pins se faaslon ka jama hamesha wohi rehta hai. Jo curve banta hai, wohi ellipse hai.
Figure 6.14 mein neela (cyan) jora aur kaala jora dekhne mein mukhtalif hain, lekin har jore ki dono lines ki lambai jama karein to total barabar aata hai. Bas yahi ek fixed total poori definition hai.
Kepler ka law aasaan alfaaz mein: planet Sun ke gird bilkul gol circle mein nahi, balke ellipse par ghoomta hai, aur Sun us ellipse ke ek focus par hota hai.
Khud sochiye: agar dono pins ek hi jagah gaar dein to pencil kaun si shakal banayegi? (Jawab: circle. Yeh baat 6.4.1 mein phir aayegi.)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Circle aur ellipse ka farq ek line mein: circle mein har point ka ek fixed point (centre) se faasla barabar hota hai, jab ke ellipse mein har point ke do fixed points (foci) se faaslon ka jama barabar hota hai. Ek point ki jagah do points, aur akele faasle ki jagah faaslon ka jama: bas itna sa farq hai.
Parabola se farq: parabola mein ek focus aur ek directrix (seedhi line) thi aur dono se faasle barabar the. Ellipse ki pehli definition mein directrix nahi, do foci hain. (6.4.1 mein ellipse ki ek doosri definition bhi aayegi jis mein directrix hoti hai.)
Is sabaq ka plan: pehle definition, phir axes ka munasib intikhab (choice), phir distance formula, do dafa square karna, aur aakhir mein \(b\) ka naya naam. Har qadam ke saath hum yeh bhi dekhenge ke woh qadam kyun uthaya gaya.
Derivation of the Standard Equation

Ab hum ellipse ki sab se saada equation banayenge. Pehle sawal: axes kahan rakhein? Hum foci ko x-axis par \(F'(-c, 0)\) aur \(F(c, 0)\) par rakhte hain, taa ke origin dono foci ko jorne wale segment ka midpoint (beech ka point) ho. Neeche Figure 6.15 dekhiye. Ellipse par kisi bhi point \(P(x, y)\) ke dono foci se faaslon ke constant jama ko hum \(2a\) kehte hain, jahan \(a > 0\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "see Figure 17" likhti hai aur aage "triangle PF'F in Figure 17" bhi. Dono jagah sahi figure Figure 6.15 hai (neeche).

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par cyan ellipse jis ka centre O magenta X aur Y axes ke origin par hai. x-axis par foci F'(-c, 0) aur F(c, 0); ellipse ka point P(x, y) dono foci se kaali lines se jura hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.15: foci at F'(-c, 0) and F(c, 0), point P(x, y) (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.15)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Foci ko \((\pm c, 0)\) par hi kyun rakha? Is tarah centre origin par aa jata hai aur ellipse dono axes ke gird symmetric (dono taraf barabar) ho jata hai. Natija yeh ke aakhri equation mein na koi akela \(x\) wala term hoga, na akela \(y\) wala, na \(xy\). Baaqi har ellipse isi ko khiska (shift) kar ke milta hai, jo hum 6.4.2 ke Theorem 1 aur 2 mein dekhenge.
Jama ko sirf \(a\) ke bajaye \(2a\) kyun kaha? Kyunke aage pata chalega ke \(a\) centre se vertex tak ka faasla hai. 2 ka factor rakhne se aakhri formula saaf suthra aata hai.
To ellipse ke har point \(P(x, y)\) ke liye yeh shart (condition) hai:

blocks.text_alt: distance P F dash plus distance P F equals 2 a

blocks.text:
Ab distance formula lagate hain. Yaad kijiye: do points \((x_1, y_1)\) aur \((x_2, y_2)\) ka faasla \(\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\) hota hai. \(P(x, y)\) se \(F'(-c, 0)\) tak faasla \(\sqrt{(x+c)^2+y^2}\) aur \(F(c, 0)\) tak \(\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\) hai. Is liye:
\[\sqrt{(x+c)^2+y^2} + \sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\]
\[= 2a\]
Do square roots ek saath hain. Inhein khatam karne ke liye ek root ko akela (isolate) kar ke ek taraf rakhte hain, phir dono sides ka square lete hain:
\[\sqrt{(x+c)^2+y^2}\]
\[= 2a - \sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\]
Square karne se (right side par \((p-q)^2 = p^2 - 2pq + q^2\) laga kar):
\[(x+c)^2+y^2\]
\[= 4a^2 - 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\]
\[\qquad + (x-c)^2 + y^2\]
Ab dono taraf ke squares khol dete hain (expand):
\[x^2+2cx+c^2+y^2\]
\[= 4a^2 - 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\]
\[\qquad + x^2-2cx+c^2+y^2\]
\(x^2\), \(c^2\) aur \(y^2\) dono taraf hain, is liye cancel ho jate hain:
\[2cx = 4a^2 - 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2} - 2cx\]
\(cx\) wale terms ek taraf jama karte hain:
\[4cx = 4a^2 - 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\]
4 se divide kar ke bacha hua root akela karte hain:
\[a\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2} = a^2 - cx\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein \(\sqrt{(x+c)^2+y^2} = 2a - \sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\) wali line ke aakhir mein ek faltu square root ka nishaan \(\sqrt{\ }\) chhapa hai. Yeh printing ki ghalti hai, is ka koi matlab nahi; equation \(\sqrt{(x-c)^2+y^2}\) par khatam hoti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehle ek root ko akela kyun kiya? Agar \(\sqrt{A} + \sqrt{B} = 2a\) ko seedha square karein to \(A + B + 2\sqrt{AB} = 4a^2\) milta hai, yani ek naya aur ziyada mushkil root \(\sqrt{AB}\) aa jata hai. Jab har side par ek hi root ho, to square karne se left wala root poori tarah khatam ho jata hai aur right par sirf ek root bachta hai.
Pehli dafa square karne ke baad bhi ek root baqi tha, is liye usay phir akela kiya, taa ke doosri dafa square kar ke woh bhi khatam ho jaye. Yeh 'akela karo, square karo' wala tareeqa har us equation mein kaam aata hai jis mein do roots hon.
Khud sochiye: \(-2cx\) right side se left par gaya to \(+2cx\) kyun ban gaya? (Side badalne par sign badalta hai.)

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: The word “focus” means "fireplace" in Latin.

Ab doosri dafa dono sides ka square lete hain. Left side par \(a^2\) aur bracket ka square, right side par \((a^2 - cx)^2\):
\[a^2\left[(x-c)^2+y^2\right]\]
\[= a^4 - 2a^2cx + c^2x^2\]
Left side ko khol kar:
\[a^2(x^2-2cx+c^2+y^2)\]
\[= a^4 - 2a^2cx + c^2x^2\]
\[a^2x^2 - 2a^2cx + a^2c^2 + a^2y^2\]
\[= a^4 - 2a^2cx + c^2x^2\]
Dekhiye, \(-2a^2cx\) dono taraf hai, cancel ho gaya:
\[a^2x^2 + a^2c^2 + a^2y^2 = a^4 + c^2x^2\]
Terms ko tarteeb dete hain: \(x^2\) wale left par, constants right par:
\[a^2x^2 - c^2x^2 + a^2y^2 = a^4 - a^2c^2\]
\[(a^2-c^2)x^2 + a^2y^2 = a^2(a^2-c^2)\]

Ab Figure 6.15 ka triangle \(PF'F\) dekhiye. Triangle ki koi do sides mil kar teesri side se lambi hoti hain, is liye \(|PF'| + |PF| > |F'F|\), yani \(2a > 2c\). Is se \(a > c\) aur \(a^2 - c^2 > 0\). Asaani ke liye hum ek naya constant \(b\) bana lete hain jis ke liye \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(b\) kyun banaya? Sirf equation ko khoobsurat aur chhota karne ke liye. \(a^2 - c^2\) positive hai, to yeh kisi positive number ka square zaroor hai; usi number ka naam \(b\) rakh diya. Aage aap dekhenge ke \(b\) centre se chhoti axis ke kinare tak ka faasla hai.
Misaal ke taur par: agar dhaage ka total \(2a = 10\) aur pins ka faasla \(2c = 8\) ho, to \(a = 5\), \(c = 4\) aur \(b^2 = 25 - 16 = 9\), yani \(b = 3\).

\(a^2 - c^2\) ki jagah \(b^2\) rakhne se ellipse ki equation yeh ban jati hai:
\[b^2x^2 + a^2y^2 = a^2b^2\]
Aakhir mein dono sides ko \(a^2b^2\) se divide karte hain, taa ke right side par 1 aa jaye. Yahi ellipse ki standard form hai:

blocks.text_alt: x squared over a squared plus y squared over b squared equals 1

blocks.text: Kyunke \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2\) aur \(a > c\), is liye \(a > b\) bhi lazmi hai. Yani is form mein bara denominator \(a^2\) hamesha \(x^2\) ke neeche hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Aaiye poori derivation ko ek nazar mein dobara dekhte hain, taa ke tareeqa zehan mein beth jaye. Shuru mein humare paas sirf definition thi: dono foci se faaslon ka jama \(2a\). Distance formula ne is definition ko do square roots wali equation bana diya.
Pehla qadam: ek root akela kiya aur square kiya. Is se ek root khatam hua, aur \(x^2\), \(c^2\), \(y^2\) cancel ho gaye. Doosra qadam: bacha hua root akela kiya aur phir square kiya. Ab koi root nahi bacha.
Teesra qadam: terms ko tarteeb di aur \(a^2 - c^2\) ko \(b^2\) ka naam diya. Chautha qadam: \(a^2b^2\) se divide kar ke right side par 1 laya. Bas, standard form tayyar.
Yeh tareeqa sirf yahan nahi, hyperbola (6.5) ki derivation mein bhi bilkul isi tarah chalta hai; wahan faaslon ka jama nahi balke farq (difference) hota hai. Is liye yeh chaar qadam achhi tarah samajh lijiye, aage bohat kaam aayenge.
Khud sochiye: agar \(c = 0\) ho (dono foci origin par) to \(b^2 = a^2\) ho jata hai aur equation \(x^2 + y^2 = a^2\) ban jati hai. Yeh kaun si shakal hai? Haan, circle! Yani circle ellipse ki ek khaas surat hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Foci \((\pm 4, 0)\) aur faaslon ka jama 10 ho to ellipse kya hoga? \(2a = 10\) se \(a = 5\), \(c = 4\), \(b^2 = 25 - 16 = 9\). Equation: \(\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1\).
Tasdeeq: point \((5, 0)\) lein. Is ka \(F'(-4, 0)\) se faasla 9 aur \(F(4, 0)\) se faasla 1 hai; jama \(9 + 1 = 10\). Bilkul sahi.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
Ellipse: har point ke dono foci se faaslon ka jama ek hi constant \(2a\) hota hai.
Foci \((\pm c, 0)\) hon to equation \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) hai, jahan \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2\).
Hamesha \(a > c\) aur \(a > b\): teeno lengths mein \(a\) sab se bari hai.
Derivation mein do dafa square kiya, aur har dafa pehle ek root ko akela kiya.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
\(b^2 = a^2 + c^2\) likh dena (yeh hyperbola ka rishta hai). Ellipse mein \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) hai, yani \(c\) hamesha \(a\) se chhota.
\(\sqrt{A} + \sqrt{B}\) ka square \(A + B\) likh dena: beech wala term \(2\sqrt{AB}\) hamesha aata hai. Isi liye pehle ek root ko akela karte hain.
Distance formula mein \(F'(-c, 0)\) ke liye \((x - c)^2\) likh dena; minus ka minus plus ban kar \((x + c)^2\) aata hai.
